articles.title: Flight disruptions continue after FAA lifts ground stop, some college football games delayed
articles.description: U.S. flights are resuming after the FAA ground stop, but delays and cancellations are still piling up.

articles.title: Interest rate rises likely in coming months, Bank of England economist says
articles.description: ‘We have further to go,’ says Huw Pill after increase to 4% last month as Bank seeks to tackle rising inflation The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said. Signalling a sharp rise in mortgage payments for an estimated 2.3 million homeowners who will have to refinance their loans next year, Huw Pill said that while the decision to nudge interest rates from 3.75% to 4% earlier this month was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, “we ⁠have further to go”.

articles.title: Health is wealth? Polymarket and Kalshi now host bets on measles and other US health crises
articles.description: Experts warn of risks of platforms hosting bets tied to US public health – including vaccine mandates and drug trials The sign was pasted on a construction fence next to an elementary school in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. “Vaccines,” it proclaimed in bold capital letters against a blue star-spangled background – appearing, at first glance, to be like any other public health message on the importance of getting vaccinated. But at the bottom of the sign, in smaller letters, it read: “Will any state end vaccine markets?” It was accompanied by the logo for Polymarket, an online prediction market where users can log in to wager on the outcomes of nearly any event – including, now, public health.

articles.title: ‘Enough is enough’: rising number of deadly ebike battery fires spark fear in New York City
articles.description: City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York, causing deaths and fear among residents, but the city has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce the threat. New York has seen a dramatic uptick this year in fires from the batteries. In 2025, there were 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death, according to the New York fire department (FDNY). This year, there have already been more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths.

articles.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage hits governments
articles.description: Tech company says operations restored to all customers and regions affected by one of worst IT failures in years Microsoft has said its service has been fully restored after a massive outage that saw widespread disruption to governments, businesses and public services around the world. The technology company said on Saturday morning it had restored service to the remaining customers affected by one of the worst IT failures in years. On its Microsoft 365 status page, the US-based firm said: “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions.

articles.title: Eisenkot condemns Netanyahu’s ‘racist’ campaign against Israel’s Arab citizens
articles.description: Prime ministerial hopeful calls Arab minority ‘an integral part of the Israeli story’ as he seeks to form government Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence. Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence.

articles.title: SpaceX not being honest about ‘political’ reasons for slowing Starshield, says Zelenskyy
articles.description: Throttling of Elon Musk’s military-grade satellite system affecting whole frontline, says Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused SpaceX of not telling the truth over restrictions to Ukraine’s Starshield satellite system , saying the decision to impose speed limits appears to be “political” rather than “technical”. Speaking on Friday, Ukraine’s president said the restrictions affecting Ukrainian drones had been in place for five days. They could no longer fly at speeds of more than 161km/h (100mph), he said, with connections at higher speeds lost.

articles.title: ‘We must deliver’: jubilant Democrats gather in Denver to chart way forward
articles.description: At party’s ‘What’s Next’ conference, consensus is they need to act quickly, but over affordability or accountability is the question What’s next for Democrats? It’s the question thousands of Democrats, including lawmakers, strategists, pollsters, creators, organizers, staffers and 2028 presidential hopefuls are trying to answer at a three-day gathering in Denver, after a sweeping victory in the 2026 midterm elections.

articles.title: Greenpeace boulders may delay building of £12bn windfarms in North Sea
articles.description: Activists dumped rocks off Norfolk coast on site of Burnham-backed project in protest against seabed trawling The giant offshore windfarms backed by Andy Burnham this week may face unexpected stumbling blocks after Greenpeace activists unwittingly dumped about 15 tonnes of boulders on to the site as part of a campaign against seabed trawling in the North Sea. Greenpeace created the “boulder barrier” to safeguard harbour porpoises off the Norfolk coast by dropping giant stone blocks, each weighing up to 2 tonnes, on to the sea floor to prevent a method of fishing known as bottom trawling.

articles.title: Torture survivors may have been sent to Sussex asylum camp unlawfully, documentary reveals
articles.description: Undercover ITV report also shows inadequate welfare checks at ex-military base run by firm of asylum camp billionaire Graham King Asylum seekers accommodated at a controversial military base in East Sussex have been subjected to inadequate welfare checks, and torture survivors may have been placed there unlawfully, a new undercover documentary for ITV has revealed. Mass accommodation sites are central to the government’s plan to end the use of hotels to house asylum seekers. For the documentary Inside The Asylum Camp, ITV’s undercover reporter got a job as a welfare officer at Crowborough and covertly filmed inside the former military training camp. The documentary claims that poor screening and welfare checks are having serious consequences for some of the asylum seekers.

articles.title: Will Trump’s lame duck presidency push him further beyond constraints of the law?
articles.description: Midterm elections have defanged the US president – leaving critics to worry about his next move in his ‘fat Elvis’ stage It was just before 3am when Donald Trump entered a crowded Manhattan ballroom, greeted by chants of “USA! USA” and theme music from the Hollywood film Air Force One. On stage, two red “Make America great again” (Maga) caps were mounted in glass cases like holy relics. That was the scene 10 years ago this week when Trump, a businessman and reality TV star, stunned the world by beating Hillary Clinton to the White House. A decade later an unlikely president is serving an unlikely second term. But in the wake of a humiliating vote of no confidence in last week’s midterm elections , he now enters an endgame wracked with uncertainty.

articles.title: Noel Fielding ‘horrified and deeply disturbed’ by Russell Brand’s crimes
articles.description: Comedian regrets ‘inappropriate’ jokes he made with Brand during work pair did together in the 2000s The Great British Bake Off presenter Noel Fielding has said he was “horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand’s crimes” and has had no contact with his fellow comedian “for many years”. In the early 2000s, Fielding often worked with Brand, who was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison on Monday for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

articles.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
articles.description: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations. After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.

articles.description: In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies. Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines. UK | Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand. Climate | The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country. US midterms | Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states. Europe | Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years , setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power. Technology | Police officers risk arresting innocent people , especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.

articles.title: 中美能源大戰，如何影響你的帳單？
articles.description: 中美之間的博弈可能會對能源成本產生重大影響，但誰會最終獲勝？

articles.title: Two skulls likely belonging to enslaved people returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies
articles.description: Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday. The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century. One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonies in both cities.

articles.title: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina
articles.description: Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody A 74-year-old former member of Italy ’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina , the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony. Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. He had received the sentence in 1987 for joining a subversive association and belonging to an armed group.

articles.title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case
articles.description: Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceans Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici , Argentina has told an international tribunal. Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.

articles.title: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
articles.description: Tomás Beltrán was shot dead amid gang warfare that has turned Latin American country into one of its most violent Tomás Beltrán was manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night when the Ecuadorian journalist was shot dead. Beltrán ran a Facebook page with news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí, whose Pacific coastline has made it a key flashpoint in the gang warfare over drug trafficking routes that has transformed one of Latin America’s safest countries into one of its most violent .

articles.title: 「中國間諜案」獲撤控男子BBC專訪：我是情報部門的替罪羊
articles.description: BBC取得並查閱的數千則訊息顯示，一名中國官員曾設法了解多項敏感政治事務的內情。

articles.title: 黃仁勳疑落入間諜戰「美人計」——韓國也曾中招
articles.description: 黃仁勳的婚外情對象被懷疑是中國間諜，使「美人計」再度受到關注。在韓國，朝鮮特工元正花曾利用與軍官的關係蒐集軍事情報。

articles.title: 認識史蒂芬妮·凱斯——首位在南極洲跑完100英里的女性
articles.description: 史蒂芬妮·凱斯創造了歷史，成為第一個完成南極洲100英里極限賽的女性。

articles.title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian prisoner of war amid surge in Russian recruitment
articles.description: Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation. The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians.

articles.title: 「台灣之光」形象重挫？民眾如何看黃仁勳婚外情風波
articles.description: 輝達（英偉達）執行長黃仁勳捲入婚外情風波，部分美國媒體引述情報官員指，涉事女子與中國情報系統有關。BBC中文在台北街頭採訪民眾，了解他們如何看待這場仍在持續發醇的風波。

articles.title: 黃仁勳曾告訴我，那些關於中國與國家安全的問題
articles.description: 黃仁勳正因涉嫌與一名中國間諜出軌而接受調查，他對世界秩序的未來遠比其他科技巨頭老闆重要得多。

articles.title: 從局長下台到議會「沉默」 宏福苑大火後的政治問責與維穩邏輯
articles.description: BBC中文採訪多名政治分析人士，拆解這場善後操作背後所反映的維穩管治邏輯，以及又與即將舉行的選委會及特首選舉有何深層連結。

articles.title: 為何晚上睡前總是想吃零食？可以怎麼辦？
articles.description: 你在睡前吃甜食是有生物學原因的，但你可以改變這個習慣。

articles.title: 一名公務員如何長期瞞天過海，身兼五職？
articles.description: 卡西姆·喬杜里（Kashim Chowdhury）在三年內將納稅人的錢挪用28.4萬英鎊後，被判犯有欺詐罪。

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
articles.description: Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory. The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.

articles.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile
articles.description: Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week. Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.

articles.title: 全球最大排放國的拐點：中國煤電佔比跌破五成，碳排放幾乎停滯
articles.description: 分析指排放或已提前達峰，但新煤電機組仍大量上馬，拐點成色有待檢驗。

articles.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir
articles.description: From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says. The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi , and you can read an excerpt from the book here .)

articles.title: 父母選擇「雙人安樂死」，留下我獨自承受喪親之痛
articles.description: 簡和埃爾斯在幸福地生活了50年後，選擇接受安樂死，留下了他們唯一的孩子。

articles.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
articles.description: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.

articles.title: 間諜、線人與秘密警察：匈牙利公開共產統治時期檔案
articles.description: 匈牙利正將其完整的國家安全紀錄檔案庫上載至網上，這些檔案可能揭示在1989年前長達40年的共產主義統治期間，誰曾監視鄰居、同事、朋友和親屬。

articles.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester
articles.description: See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester. See My World , a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.

articles.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm
articles.description: Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo . A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.

articles.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.

articles.title: 美國中期選舉掀「藍色浪潮」 將怎樣影響世界
articles.description: 在剛剛結束的美國中期選舉中，多個支持共和黨的州「翻藍」，民主黨奪得國會參眾兩院控制權。這次選舉結果為何具有重大意義？又將如何影響美國與世界其他國家的關係？

articles.title: 「短睡眠基因」：為何有人只需睡四小時？
articles.description: 一般成年人平均需要七至九小時睡眠，但有些人確實只需極少睡眠也能維持良好狀態。

articles.title: 黃之鋒涉「勾結外國勢力」被重判10年 出獄或已40歲
articles.description: 上個月剛滿30歲的黃之鋒，自2020年底起因不同案件入獄，至今身在獄中超過六年。

articles.title: 從蔡康永、《VIVANT》到姆巴佩，北京為何區別處理「辱華」？
articles.description: 最近幾週，中國輿論場接連出現多宗被貼上「辱華」標籤的爭議事件：台灣藝人蔡康永、日本電視劇《VIVANT》以及法國球星姆巴佩。三宗事件看似性質相近，但官方反應與輿論熱度卻明顯不同，多位分析人士對BBC中文指出：這些差異背後是當局對於每個事件的定性並不相同。

articles.title: 他們在等西西弗斯：黃之鋒身後，那些寫信和探監的前戰友
articles.description: 香港民主派活動人士黃之鋒被控違反中國《香港國安法》下的「串謀勾結外國勢力危害國家安全」罪，被判囚10年。BBC中文訪問了三位一直探望並寄信予黃之鋒的前戰友，了解他在獄中的變化。

articles.title: 美智庫解析「技術民族主義」下的中俄軍工合作細節與限度
articles.description: 深圳APEC前夕，中俄「無上限」合有任何挑戰嗎？北京對烏克蘭停火興趣如何？在APEC中美俄三方領袖會面能有所突破？

articles.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’
articles.description: A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator. Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

articles.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying
articles.description: Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents. This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.

articles.title: Netflix 重現斯坦福監獄「虐待性」研究應該嗎？
articles.description: Netflix將美國心理學家菲利普·津巴多 (Philip Zimbardo) 1971 年備受爭議的研究改編成了一部六集真人秀，重新引發了一場由來已久的辯論，並引發了關於科學與娛樂之間界限的新問題。

articles.title: 四成「陸配」參選遭剔除，身分「法理死結」如何困住參政之路？
articles.description: 「除籍滿10年」如何計算，成為這屆選舉多位陸配被剔除參選資格的爭議焦點。今年有25位「陸配」參選，當中逾4成參選人不符參選資格。

articles.title: 「政二代」蘇巧慧對決「專業副手」李四川，誰能拿下新北？
articles.description: 作為全台人口最多的直轄市，新北市被視為「最關鍵戰場」，將判定藍綠整體勝負，並可能牽動2028年總統大選。

articles.title: 為什麼歐洲各國年輕人走上街頭？背後的共同訴求和暴力隱憂
articles.description: 過去一個月，歐洲各地爆發了由青年主導的示威遊行。這些遊行活動有何共同點？

articles.title: 「九合一」五大看點：「洋流」能否撼動台北？誰在卡位2028？
articles.description: 中共是否介入台灣選舉？ 這次選舉將如何影響賴清德與國民黨主席鄭麗文的政治能量？捲土重來、希望藉著地方議員選舉有所斬獲的小黨，此次結盟能否在主流政黨夾殺中突圍而出？

articles.title: 武契奇14年執政落幕，中塞「鐵桿友誼」何去何從？
articles.description: 從總理到總統，武契奇領導的塞爾維亞進步黨（SNS）一步步將塞爾維亞打造成歐洲強硬的親華國家，中國亦曾形容兩國關係為「鐵桿友誼 」。外界關注這一親華總統敗選，將如何改變中塞關係。

articles.title: 普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對
articles.description: 在普京建議三方於APEC期間進行會談後，特朗普表示願意參與，強調會談重點將是無核化問題。目前中方尚未就三方會談表態。

articles.title: DeepSeek被美國政府系統禁用：中美AI競爭繼續升溫
articles.description: DeepSeek的免費聊天機器人應用程式在Apple App Store下載排行榜上名列前茅，其AI模型也被美國科技企業採用。Snowflake、Vercel及OpenRouter等公司都已將DeepSeek整合至其提供給客戶的服務中。

articles.title: 台灣「北藍南綠」的政治版圖是否「鐵板一塊」？
articles.description: 「北藍南綠」是描述台灣政治版圖的常見概念，但近年選舉結果顯示，這樣的區域分野並非一成不變，中間選民的流向在這次地方選舉可能左右大局。

articles.title: 「特習會」後兩架美國 F-16V 抵台 「雖遲但到」的時機與信號
articles.description: 本周五，台灣在2019年向美國訂購的2架F-16V戰機先行抵達台灣台東空軍志航基地，同批次共有66架同型號戰機，是1990 年代以來台灣首次戰機採購。

articles.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像
articles.description: 習近平即將到訪美國會晤特朗普（川普），這將是他歷來第11次以中國官方身份訪美。從31歲縣委書記到中國國家主席，BBC中文透過歷年照片，回顧他的訪美行程如何隨身份和中美關係變化。
